description: How two devices' user states merge, and which exchange files are refused. Shared with the mobile client: both implementations must reproduce every case. Omitted in a case: empty collections, peers [], settings { residence: bizkaia, residenceHlc: null }, schemaVersion 1 and deviceName null on the incoming file, and every optional row column (null; fees and taxWithheld "0", fxSource IDENTITY, funding CASH, hedgedToBase false, thesis CORE). A merge may carry resolutions, keyed by conflictKey; an expected error means merge throws. An expected plan compares apply and effects only when it lists no conflicts, unless compareApply is true; apply.peers is compared only when the case lists it; setAside is always compared. A scenario replays syncs between devices: each step exports `from` at nowMs (exportDevice), merges it into `to` with the step's resolutions, and then: with conflicts nothing changes; with no data to change (changesData false) only the peers are written and the status is up-to-date; otherwise applyPlan at nowMs. converged: the two user states (all but deviceId and peers) end equal.
